'''Chulabhorn, Princess Srisavangavadhana'''{{efn|{{langx|th|สมเด็จพระเจ้าน้องนางเธอ เจ้าฟ้าจุฬาภรณวลัยลักษณ์ อัครราชกุมารี กรมพระศรีสวางควัฒน วรขัตติยราชนารี}}, {{IPA|th|sǒm.dèt.pʰráʔ.tɕâːw.nɔ́ːŋ.nāːŋ.tʰɤ̄ː tɕâːw.fáː.tɕù.lāː.pʰɔ̄ːn.wá.lāj.lák ʔàk.kʰrá.râːt.tɕʰā.kū.māː.rīː krōm.pʰráʔ.sǐː.sā.wǎːŋ.kʰā.wát wɔ̄ː.rā.kʰàt.tī.já.râːt.tɕʰā.nāː.rīː|pron}}}} (born 4 July 1957) is a Thai princess. She is the youngest daughter of [[King Bhumibol Adulyadej]] (Rama IX) and [[Queen Sirikit]], and the younger sister of [[King Vajiralongkorn]] (Rama X).<ref>Finestone, Jeffrey. ''The Royal Family of Thailand: The Descendants of King Chulalongkorn''. Bangkok : Phitsanulok Publishing, 1989, p. 273</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=HM The King confers new royal titles on his family - PHOTOS |url=https://thethaiger.com/hot-news/events/hm-the-king-confers-new-royal-titles-on-his-family-photos |work=Thaiger |date=6 May 2019 |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Princess Chulabhorn was born on 4 July 1957 at [[Amphorn Sathan Residential Hall]] of the [[Dusit Palace]] in Bangkok. She studied [[chemistry]] and graduated in 1979 from the Faculty of Science at [[Kasetsart University]], with a Bachelor of Science, [[British undergraduate degree classification|First Class Honours]]. She continued to study Science at [[Mahidol University]], where she received her Doctorate in 1985.

She is heavily involved in the promotion of scientific research, and regularly gives awards and prizes. She held the position of a guest lecturer in chemistry at the [[Mahidol University]]. She also serves as president of the [[Chulabhorn Research Institute]]. She was awarded the [[UNESCO]] Einstein Medal<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cri.or.th/en/pr_president.php|title=Chulabhorn Research Institute|website=Cri.or.th|access-date=30 March 2016|archive-date=5 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305051318/https://www.cri.or.th/en/pr_president.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> for her efforts in promoting scientific collaboration in 1986 and was the first Asian to be invited to join the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] in the United Kingdom as an [[Honorary Fellow]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/Membership/AboutRscMembership/HonFRSC/index.asp |title=Membership and professional community |publisher=Rsc.org |access-date=30 March 2016}}</ref>

Later in 2019, she received a Ph.D. in Visual Arts from the Faculty of Painting, Sculpture and Graphic Arts, [[Silpakorn University]].

==Personal life==
On 7 January 1982, Chulabhorn married [[Royal Thai Air Force]] officer [[Group Captain]] Virayudh Tishyasarin ({{langx|th|วีระยุทธ ดิษยะศริน}}; {{RTGS|''Wirayut Dityasarin''}}), a commoner, an [[Air vice-marshal]]. They have two children: Princess [[Siribha Chudabhorn]] and Princess [[Aditayadorn Kitikhun]]. According to royal custom, she would have lost her title upon marrying a man of lower rank. However, they divorced in February 1996, and she subsequently returned to the royal court.<ref>[https://www.upi.com/amp/Archives/1996/10/11/Thai-princess-announces-divorce/8874845006400/ Thai princess announces divorce]</ref>
	
She resides at Chakri Bongkot Palace.

==Official duties==
The Princess visited [[Germany]] from 13 to 15 April 2010. During her visit she went to the [[German Cancer Research Center]] in [[Heidelberg]] to further her [[cancer]] research and to learn more about the developments the center had found. Princess Chulabhorn had visited the center already in 1986, 1995 and 2000.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dkfz.de/en/presse/pressemitteilungen/2010/dkfz_pm_10_14.php|title=Royal Visitor at the German Cancer Research Center: Princess of Thailand Visits Heidelberg|date=13 April 2010|access-date=23 December 2023|website=Deutsches Krebsforschungszentrum}}</ref>

In November 2016, Princess Chulabhorn visited Japan and met with then-[[Emperor Akihito]] and then-[[Empress Michiko]] at the [[Tokyo Imperial Palace|Imperial Palace]], [[Tokyo]]. The Imperial couple hosted a luncheon in her honor.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/1143697|title=HRH Chulabhorn meets Japan's Akihito|date=25 November 2016|access-date=8 December 2023|website=Bangkok Post}}</ref> During her visit to the country, The Princess went to [[Nagoya University]], in [[Aichi Prefecture]], to take part in a discussion between the "HRH Princess Chulabhorn College of Medical Science" in [[Thailand]] and the "School of Medicine" in the university.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://en.nagoya-u.ac.jp/news/hrh_princess_chulabhorn_of_thailand_visits_nagoya_university.html|title=HRH Princess Chulabhorn of Thailand Visits Nagoya University|date=22 November 2016|access-date=8 December 2023|website=Nagoya University official website}}</ref>

In March 2023, Princess Chulabhorn officially visited [[Israel]]: during the visit she toured the [[Hadassah Ein Kerem hospital]], in [[Jerusalem]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/israel/diplomacy/1679587176-thailand-s-princess-chulabhorn-mahidol-jerusalem-hospital|title=Thailand's Princess Chulabhorn Mahidol visits Jerusalem Hospital|date=23 March 2023|access-date=2 December 2023|website=i24 News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hadassahinternational.org/interest-in-cancer-treatment-brings-thailand-princess-to-hadassah/|title=INTEREST IN CANCER TREATMENT BRINGS THAILAND PRINCESS TO HADASSAH|date=26 March 2023|access-date=2 December 2023|website=Hadassah International.org}}</ref> Additionally, the Princess visited "[[Israel Diamond Exchange]]" with the Thai ambassador to Israel, [[Pannabha Chandraramya]]. At the event, Princess Chulabhorn discussed relations between [[Thailand]] and Israel. The president of the association, Boaz Moldawsky participated with the Princess in a ceremony in honor of the association.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.en.isde.co.il/article.aspx?id=35760|title=Thai Princess visit ISDE|date=14 March 2023|access-date=2 December 2023|website=Israel Diamond Exchange}}</ref> During her visit to the country, the Princess went to the [[Western Wall]] (also called as the Wailing Wall), in [[Jerusalem]], to pray. She also learned the importance of that monument to the country.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thekotel.org/en/131118/|title=Royal Visit at the Western Wall: The Princess of Thailand Comes to the Wall to Visit and Pray|date=15 March 2023|access-date=2 December 2023|website=The Western Wall Heritage Foundation}}</ref><br> In April 2023, Princess Chulabhorn visited the [[United States of America]] to attend the Health Summit for Pharmaceutical and Medical Development at [[Tufts University]] in [[Massachusetts]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://now.tufts.edu/2023/04/26/summit-highlights-strengths-one-health-approaches-medicine|title=Summit Highlights Strengths of One Health Approaches to Medicine|date=26 April 2023|access-date=23 December 2023|website=Tufts Now}}</ref> The Princess also toured the institute and subsequently visited the [[Frederick National Laboratory for Cancer Research|NCI Frederick Campus]] in [[Maryland]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nihrecord.nih.gov/thai-princess-visits-nci-frederick-campus|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230531010426/https://nihrecord.nih.gov/thai-princess-visits-nci-frederick-campus|url-status=dead|archive-date=31 May 2023|title=Thai Princess Visits NCI Frederick Campus|date=21 April 2023|access-date=23 December 2023|website=NIH Record}}</ref><br>
In June 2023 Princess Chulabhorn also paid an official visit to [[Mongolia]]: during the visit she received an [[honorary Doctorate]] from the [[Mongolian University of Life Sciences]], during the Princess's visit to the university headquarters in [[Ulaanbaatar]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://muls.edu.mn/view_news.php?value_id=ZW5jb2RldXNlcmlkMzYwNQ==|title=ТАЙЛАНДЫН ХААНТ УЛСЫН ЭРХЭМСЭГ ГҮНЖ ЧУЛАБХОРН СРИСАВАНГАВАДХАВАД ХААИС-ИЙН ХҮНДЭТ ДОКТОР ЦОЛ ОЛГОВ|date=28 June 2023|access-date=2 December 2023|website=ХААИС|language=mn}}</ref>

==Health==
On 6 September 2014, the Princess was admitted to [[Vichaiyut Hospital]] due to stomach inflammation: she was later diagnosed with [[gastritis]] and was advised to temporarily suspend royal duties.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/430816/princess-treated-for-stomach-pain|title=Princess Chulabhorn in hospital|date=6 September 2014|access-date=7 December 2023|website=Bangkok Post}}</ref> 

On 9 October 2014, the Princess was diagnosed with a severe infection of the [[pancreas]] and swelling of the lymph glands: doctors concluded that she was suffering from an autoimmune disease called [[systemic lupus erythematosus]], which she has since begun to treat. Doctors advised her to stop activities for three months. She had been in hospital since the previous September.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.khaosodenglish.com/life/2014/10/09/1412848613/|title=HM KING'S DAUGHTER SUFFERS FROM AUTO-IMMUNE DISEASE, PALACE SAYS|date=9 October 2014|access-date=7 December 2023|website=Khaosod English}}</ref> 

On 5 November 2015, Princess Chulabhorn underwent surgery at Vichaiyut hospital to remove seven [[polyps]] from her large intestine. A blood test had previously shown that the princess had a higher than normal level of [[carcinoembryonic antigen]] which indicated that she was likely to develop [[cancer]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/755692/princess-chulabhorn-recovers-after-operation|title=Princess Chulabhorn recovers after operation|date=5 November 2015|access-date=7 December 2023|website=Bangkok Post}}</ref> 

In May 2016, the Princess was found to have a non-malignant [[tumor]] in her neck, and it was removed at Vichaiyut Hospital. She had to suspend her official duties to recover after the operation and to treat her [[pancreatitis]], which she had been suffering from for a while and which was causing some health problems to her.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/992405/princess-chulabhorn-resting-after-surgery|title=Princess resting after successful surgery|date=28 May 2016|access-date=8 December 2023|website=Bangkok Post}}</ref> As of July 2016, her pancreatitis was becoming intermittent and acute, a sign that it was worsening over time. To receive treatment, the Princess had to suspend her official commitments until she recovered.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/1042117/princess-suffers-acute-pancreatitis|title=Princess suffers acute pancreatitis|date=23 July 2016|access-date=8 December 2023|website=Bangkok Post}}</ref> 

In June 2017, the Princess was diagnosed with lung, liver and muscle inflammation and low blood oxygen levels: she went to Vichaiyuth Hospital due to fatigue, shortness of breath and other symptoms and doctors made the diagnosis, and subsequently administered medical treatment to her.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thailandnews.co/2017/06/princess-chulabhorn-vichaiyuth-hospital-condition-improved/|title=Princess Chulabhorn in Vichaiyuth hospital, but her condition has improved|date=23 June 2017|access-date=9 December 2023|website=Thailand News}}</ref> 

In February 2019, Princess Chulabhorn was admitted to [[Ramathibodi Hospital]] in [[Bangkok]] after developing back pain and blurred vision in both eyes. Doctors concluded that further tests were necessary and the Princess extended her stay in hospital.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/1623906|title=HRH Princess Chulabhorn is in hospital|date=5 February 2019|access-date=7 December 2023|website=Bangkok Post}}</ref> 

In April 2019, Chulabhorn underwent surgery to remove [[cataracts]] (which had caused blurred vision) and underwent treatment for her newly diagnosed back infection (which caused back pain). Her recovery was confirmed a few days later.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.khaosodenglish.com/news/2019/04/15/kings-sister-recovering-from-back-infection-palace-says/|title=KING'S SISTER RECOVERING FROM BACK INFECTION, PALACE SAYS|date=15 April 2019|access-date=7 December 2023|website=Khaosod English}}</ref> 

On 30 September 2019, Chulabhorn went to [[Chulabhorn Hospital]] after experiencing numbness in her left hand. An [[MRI]] showed that the nerves under her left elbow had become compressed, and as a result the Princess had to remain in hospital for treatment and suspend royal duties.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thaipbsworld.com/princess-chulabhorn-in-hospital-to-treat-numbness-in-her-hand/|title=Princess Chulabhorn in hospital to treat numbness in her hand|date=1 October 2019|access-date=9 December 2023|website=Thai PBS World}}</ref> As a result of numbness in her left hand, Chulabhorn had to undergo [[microsurgery]] to remove the tissue causing the discomfort and remained in hospital until she fully recovered.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thaipbsworld.com/princess-chulabhorn-is-recuperating-in-hospital-after-surgery-to-treat-numbness-in-left-hand/|title=Princess Chulabhorn is recuperating in hospital after surgery to treat numbness in left hand|date=4 October 2019|access-date=9 December 2023|website=Thai PBS World}}</ref> 

On 16 June 2020, Chulabhorn underwent surgery at [[Chulalongkorn Hospital]] due to numbness in the fingertips of her right hand, caused by a membrane compressing the nerve below her elbow. She was discharged approximately fifteen days later when she was judged to have recovered.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thaipbsworld.com/princess-chulabhorn-recovers-from-surgery-and-is-discharged-from-hospital/|title=Princess Chulabhorn recovers from surgery and is discharged from hospital|date=28 June 2020|access-date=8 December 2023|website=Thai PBS World}}</ref>

In early October 2024, she had to suspend her engagements and activities for a while in order to proceed with rehabilitation, due to a surgery underwent two months earlier because of pain in her left foot and ankle at Chulabhorn Hospital in [[Lak Si district]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2876471/princess-chulabhorn-begins-post-op-therapy|title=Princess Chulabhorn begins post-op therapy|date=2 October 2024|access-date=21 October 2025|website=Bangkok Post}}</ref>

===Other honours=== 
Princess Chulabhorn received [[UNESCO]]'s Einstein Medal for her years of work promoting scientific cooperation in the Asia - Pacific region. In 2009, she received the Adolf Windaus Medal.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Öffentlichkeitsarbeit |first1=Georg-August-Universität Göttingen- |title=Presseinformationen - Georg-August-University Göttingen |url=https://www.uni-goettingen.de/en/1314.html?cid=3366 |website=Georg-August Universität Göttingen |language=de}}</ref>

Princess Chulabhorn has been an honorary member of the Society for Medicinal Plant and Natural Product Research since 1999.
